ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a common-emitter transistor circuit, with the emitter connected to the bottom common reference node; the base is fed from the left-side 5 V power supply through the Rs = 2 kΩ resistor; the collector is connected to the right-side 5 V power supply through Rc; next to the transistor is marked β = 100. The problem gives V_BE = 0.7 V, V_CE(sat) = 0.2 V. Reasoning: The base current I_B = (5 - 0.7) / 2000 = 4.3 / 2000 = 0.00215 A. To maintain the active region, the collector current is I_C = β I_B = 100 × 0.00215 = 0.215 A. The maximum value of Rc occurs when it just reaches the saturation boundary, at which time V_CE = V_CE(sat) = 0.2 V. Since the emitter is grounded, the voltage drop across Rc is 5 - 0.2 = 4.8 V. Therefore Rc_max = 4.8 / 0.215 = 22.3256 Ω, about 22.32 Ω.
